title: Embedded Systems
intro: A short, independent catch-up: learn the essential knowledge, practise and review answers.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic is typical of an embedded system?
options: It performs a dedicated function inside a larger device
It must run every desktop application
It always has a full-size keyboard
It stores data only in the cloud
questions.answer: It performs a dedicated function inside a larger device
questions.feedback: Embedded controllers perform specific jobs within devices.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the explanations, visual and model before answering.

blocks.title: Built into a larger device
blocks.text: An embedded system is a computer built into a larger device to perform a specific function. Unlike a general-purpose PC, it is designed for a particular job, such as controlling an automatic device.

blocks.title: Input → process → output
blocks.text: A sensor or switch provides an input. The embedded processor follows stored instructions to make a decision, then controls an output. The output might be a display, motor, light or heater.

blocks.title: Software and memory
blocks.text: The dedicated control program is commonly stored in non-volatile memory (such as ROM/flash) so it remains available when power is off. RAM holds temporary data while the system runs.

blocks.title: Characteristics depend on the job
blocks.text: Embedded systems often have limited user interfaces and are designed to use little power. Some must respond within a fixed time (real-time operation), for example where a delay would affect safety. Not every device has every feature.

blocks.title: Visual model
blocks.caption: Use these linked concepts to explain your answer.

blocks.title: Worked example · A washing machine uses a processor to control its wash cycle. Explain why it is an embedded system, identify a sensor input, and name an output. [4 marks]
blocks.text: Identify the machine's job: controlling the washing cycle. The controller is part of a larger washing machine, not a general-purpose computer. It is a computer built into another device [1] designed for the specific job of controlling the wash cycle [1]. A water-level sensor sends information to the controller [1]. Other relevant sensors could include temperature sensors. The controller may switch the drum motor on/off as an output [1]. Total: 4 clear marking points — larger device, dedicated purpose, input, output.

items: Embedded system — A computer built into a larger device to perform a specific function.
Dedicated function — A particular task for which a system has been designed.
Sensor — An input device that detects or measures a physical condition.
Actuator — An output device that produces a physical action, such as switching or moving a mechanism.
Real-time operation — A system responds to inputs within a required time limit.
Non-volatile memory — Memory that keeps stored information even when power is switched off.
User interface — The controls or display through which a person interacts with a system.

writing.prompt: A car-park barrier uses a vehicle sensor and a motor to lift the barrier when authorised. Explain why its controller is an embedded system, and identify an input and an output. [4 marks]
writing.model: It is a computer built into the wider barrier system [1] for the specific function of controlling entry [1]. Input: a vehicle-detection sensor [1]. Output: controlling the motor to raise/lower the barrier [1]. 'Barrier' alone is not a specific input or output.
